q-39669.name: Question 1
q-39669.problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to (x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)),$ given that 

$$
u=2x+y,\,v=-x+3y-2z,\,w=3y+4z.
$$
q-39669.worked_solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =2 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =1 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =0 \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =-1 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =3 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & =-2 \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =3 & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(12+6)-1(-4-0) \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{40}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation T:(u,v,w)→(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)), given that u=2x+y,v=−x+3y−2z,w=3y+4z.

a
40
b
8
c
16
d
140
e
116
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a transformation

T:[uvw]→[x(u,v,w)y(u,v,w)z(u,v,w)],

the Jacobian determinant of T, denoted ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w), is given by

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=|∂x∂u∂x∂v∂x∂w∂y∂u∂y∂v∂y∂w∂z∂u∂z∂v∂z∂w|.

In this case, we're only given T−1. So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of T as follows:

  • First, we compute ∂(u,v,w)∂(x,y,z), the Jacobian determinant of T−1.

  • Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of T using the relation ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=(∂(u,v,w)∂(x,y,z))−1.

First, we find the partial derivatives:

∂u∂x=2∂u∂y=1∂u∂z=0∂v∂x=−1∂v∂y=3∂v∂z=−2∂w∂x=0∂w∂y=3∂w∂z=4

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of T−1 is

∂(u,v,w)∂(x,y,z)=|∂u∂x∂u∂y∂u∂z∂v∂x∂v∂y∂v∂z∂w∂x∂w∂y∂w∂z|=|210−13−2034|=2|3−234|−1|−1−204|=2(12+6)−1(−4−0)=40.

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=(∂(u,v,w)∂(x,y,z))−1=140.

q-161802.name: Question 2
q-161802.problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to (x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)),$ given that 

$$
u=3x+yz,\,v=z,\,w=-y.
$$
q-161802.worked_solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =3 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =z & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =y \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & =1 \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =-1 & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & z & y \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =3|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(0+1) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

a
−1
b
−3
c
−13
d
3
e

Correct
EXPLANATION

For a transformation T:[uvw]→[x(u,v,w)y(u,v,w)z(u,v,w)],

the Jacobian determinant of T, denoted ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w), is given by

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=|∂x∂u∂x∂v∂x∂w∂y∂u∂y∂v∂y∂w∂z∂u∂z∂v∂z∂w|.

In this case, we're only given T−1. So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of T as follows:

  • First, we compute ∂(u,v,w)∂(x,y,z), the Jacobian determinant of T−1.

  • Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of T using the relation ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=(∂(u,v,w)∂(x,y,z))−1.

First, we find the partial derivatives:

∂u∂x=3∂u∂y=z∂u∂z=y∂v∂x=0∂v∂y=0∂v∂z=1∂w∂x=0∂w∂y=−1∂w∂z=0

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of T−1 is

∂(u,v,w)∂(x,y,z)=|∂u∂x∂u∂y∂u∂z∂v∂x∂v∂y∂v∂z∂w∂x∂w∂y∂w∂z|=|3zy0010−10|=3|01−10|=3(0+1)=3

Finally, we take the reciprocal: ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=(∂(u,v,w)∂(x,y,z))−1=13

q-161811.name: Question 3
q-161811.problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{e}^{u}+v \\ v+w \\ vw\end{aligned}].
$$
q-161811.worked_solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)={e}^{u}+v,\,y(u,v,w)=v+w,\,z(u,v,w)=vw.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & ={e}^{u} & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =1 & \,\frac{∂x}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =0 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂w} & =1 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =0 & \,\frac{∂z}{∂v} & =w & \,\frac{∂z}{∂w} & =v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}{e}^{u} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & w & v\end{aligned}| \\  & ={e}^{u}|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ w & v\end{aligned}| \\  & ={e}^{u}(v-w).\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =0 \\ {e}^{u}(v-w) & =0 \\ v-w & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $v-w=0$ defines the plane $v=w.$

choices.value: The critical points lie on the $vw-$plane.

q-161811.html:
Question 3
?

Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation T, where T is defined as

T:[uvw]⟶[eu+vv+wvw].

a
The critical points lie on the vw−plane.
b
The critical points lie on the uv−plane.
c
The critical points lie on the sphere x2+y2+z2=4.
d
The critical points lie on the plane v=w.
e
The critical points lie on the parabolic cylinder v=2w2.
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a transformation

T:[uvw]→[x(u,v,w)y(u,v,w)z(u,v,w)],

the Jacobian determinant of T, denoted ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w), is given by

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=|∂x∂u∂x∂v∂x∂w∂y∂u∂y∂v∂y∂w∂z∂u∂z∂v∂z∂w|.

Here, we have

x(u,v,w)=eu+v,y(u,v,w)=v+w,z(u,v,w)=vw.

First, we find the partial derivatives:

∂x∂u=eu∂x∂v=1∂x∂w=0∂y∂u=0∂y∂v=1∂y∂w=1∂z∂u=0∂z∂v=w∂z∂w=v

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=|eu100110wv|=eu|11wv|=eu(v−w).

The function has critical points when ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=0. So, we obtain

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=0eu(v−w)=0v−w=0.

The equation v−w=0 defines the plane v=w.

q-161814.name: Question 4
q-161814.problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}u+2w \\ v-u \\ uw\end{aligned}].
$$
q-161814.worked_solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=u+2w,\,y(u,v,w)=v-u,\,z(u,v,w)=uw.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =1 & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =0 & \,\frac{∂x}{∂w} & =2 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =-1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =w & \,\frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0 & \,\frac{∂z}{∂w} & =u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ w & 0 & u\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & u\end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ w & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(u-0)+2(0-w) \\  & =u-2w.\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =0 \\ u-2w & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $u-2w=0$ defines the plane $u=2w.$

Question 4
?

Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation T, where T is defined as

T:[uvw]⟶[u+2wv−uuw].

a

b
The critical points lie on the plane u+v−2w=0.
c
The critical points lie on the elliptic cylinder u2+2w2=1.

The critical points lie on the vw− plane.

For a transformation

T:[uvw]→[x(u,v,w)y(u,v,w)z(u,v,w)],

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=|∂x∂u∂x∂v∂x∂w∂y∂u∂y∂v∂y∂w∂z∂u∂z∂v∂z∂w|.

Here, we have

x(u,v,w)=u+2w,y(u,v,w)=v−u,z(u,v,w)=uw.

First, we find the partial derivatives:

∂x∂u=1∂x∂v=0∂x∂w=2∂y∂u=−1∂y∂v=1∂y∂w=0∂z∂u=w∂z∂v=0∂z∂w=u

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=|102−110w0u|=1|100u|+2|−11w0|=1(u−0)+2(0−w)=u−2w.

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=0u−2w=0.

q-161818.name: Question 5
q-161818.problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}u+3w \\ v+2w \\ {v}^{2}-u\end{aligned}].
$$
q-161818.worked_solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=u+3w,\,y(u,v,w)=v+2w,\,z(u,v,w)={v}^{2}-u.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =1 & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =0 & \,\frac{∂x}{∂w} & =3 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =0 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂w} & =2 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =-1 & \,\frac{∂z}{∂v} & =2v & \,\frac{∂z}{∂w} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 2v & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2v & 0\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2v\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(0-4v)+3(0+1) \\  & =3-4v.\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =0 \\ 3-4v & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $3-4v=0$ defines the plane $v=\frac{3}{4}.$

q-161818.html:
Question 5
?

Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation T, where T is defined as

T:[uvw]⟶[u+3wv+2wv2−u].

a
 The critical points lie on the plane v=34.
b
 The critical points lie on the parabolic cylinder w=v22.
c
 The critical points lie on the uw− plane.
d
 The critical points lie on the planes v=±w.
e
 The critical points lie on the plane v=u.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a transformation

T:[uvw]→[x(u,v,w)y(u,v,w)z(u,v,w)],

the Jacobian determinant of T, denoted ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w), is given by

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=|∂x∂u∂x∂v∂x∂w∂y∂u∂y∂v∂y∂w∂z∂u∂z∂v∂z∂w|.

Here, we have

x(u,v,w)=u+3w,y(u,v,w)=v+2w,z(u,v,w)=v2−u.

First, we find the partial derivatives:

∂x∂u=1∂x∂v=0∂x∂w=3∂y∂u=0∂y∂v=1∂y∂w=2∂z∂u=−1∂z∂v=2v∂z∂w=0

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=|103012−12v0|=1|122v0|+3|01−12v|=1(0−4v)+3(0+1)=3−4v.

The function has critical points when ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=0. So, we obtain

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=03−4v=0.

The equation 3−4v=0 defines the plane v=34.
